subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Edison vs. Ford
description: A quick win: understand Edison vs. Ford.

hook.text: Thomas Edison and Henry Ford were close friends. But they bet on very different futures.

buildup.text: Edison spent years trying to build a better battery for electric cars. Ford built gasoline Model Ts.

discovery.text: Edison's nickel-iron battery was durable but too heavy and expensive for practical cars.

twist.text: Ford's cheap gasoline cars won the market. Even Edison's lab fire in 1914 slowed his battery work.

climax.text: Edison eventually gave up on electric cars. Gasoline dominated for the next hundred years.

punchline.text: The greatest inventor of his age lost the car battle.

quiz.question: Why did Edison's electric car battery fail commercially?
options: It was too heavy and expensive

details.summary: Thomas Edison and Henry Ford were close friends who nearly collaborated on an electric car in 1914, but Ford chose gasoline for the Model T because batteries could not match the range and refueling speed of gas.
details.whyItMatters: History might have been very different if Edison's batteries had met Ford's requirements. The failure of early electric car collaboration set the stage for a century of gasoline dominance.
takeaways: Edison spent years developing a better battery for electric cars
Ford initially planned an affordable electric car with Edison
Gasoline's energy density won out over early battery technology

faq.question: How close did Edison and Ford come to building an electric car?
faq.answer: Ford reportedly invested $1.5 million in the project and Edison built prototype batteries. But the batteries could not achieve sufficient range or durability, and Ford moved forward with the gasoline-powered Model T instead.

faq.question: Could early electric cars have worked with better batteries?
faq.answer: Possibly. If battery energy density had matched gasoline's energy content, the infrastructure for electric cars might have developed alongside roads. But the physics gap between battery and gasoline energy storage was simply too large.
